title: Annotatio IV §.XI open: Seventh century — Mejerus; few truth-witnesses; sterile age
pass_a_gloss: §. XI. What it is lawful for us to hope concerning the SEVENTH AGE, as to confirmation of the Eucharistic truth, the Inscription prefixed in this manner by Mejerus of Helmstedt, just now cited, sets in the open: To the seventh age, by the common sentence of Protestant doctors, are referred the beginnings of Anti-Christ, both Eastern and Western: Whence in this age the State of the Christian Religion suffered notable changes. And indeed in the East there occurred not so much some heresy or sect as the ruin of the whole Christian Religion. In the West the Roman Pontiffs, by Antichristian domination, strive to make the hitherto freer state of the Church of the Christian Religion now servile (§. 1. 52. p. 170). To which prefixed Inscription let there be added the suffix of the third Paragraph: The witnesses of Truth who in this age contradicted the mystery of iniquity and propagated the sincerity of the Christian Religion were exceedingly few in number, and even some of them inept questions occupied and exercised, necessary doctrine neglected: For the VIIth Age is sterile of writers of good fruit (p. m. 171).
pass_b_english: §.XI: what hope for the SEVENTH age confirming Eucharistic truth? Mejerus puts it in the open.

Protestant doctors refer Anti-Christ’s beginnings (East and West) to this age — East: ruin of whole religion; West: Rome drives the Church toward servitude. Truth-witnesses few; Age VII sterile of good writers.
source_text: §. XI. De SECULO SEPTIMO quid nobis sperare liceat, quod ad confirmationem veritatis Eucharisticæ attinet, in aprico ponit Inscriptio à paulò ante allegato Mejero Helmstadiensi, eidem, hunc in modum, præfixa: In seculum septimum, communi doctorum Protestantium sententia, referuntur initia Anti-Christi, tam Orientalis quam Occidentalis: Unde insignes hôc seculo Status Religionis Christianæ passus est mutationes. Et quidem in Oriente non tam hæresis aliqua, aut secta, sed totius Religionis Christianæ occurrit excidium. In Occidente Pontifices Romani, Antichristiana dominatione statum Ecclesiæ Religionis Christianæ hactenus liberiorem, nunc servilem facere satagunt. §. 1. 52. p. 170. Cui præfixæ Inscriptioni accedat suffixa Paragraphi tertii: Veritatis testes, qui hoc seculo, mysterio iniquitatis contradixerunt, & Religionis Christianæ sinceritatem propagaverunt, numero oppido pauci fuerunt, quorum etiam aliquos ineptæ quæstiones occuparunt & exercuerunt, necessariâ doctrina neglectâ: Est enim Seculum VII. sterile scriptorum bonæ frugis. p. m. 171.
